task.title: Expiring bounded work queue
task.specification: Config capacity>=1. Start now=0 and empty jobs. Events: add{id,size>0,deadline>=0}, cancel{id}, advance{dt>=0}, run. Advance adds dt; before processing any other event remove jobs with deadline<=now (also remove immediately after advance). Add succeeds only if id is not currently queued, deadline>now and total size+size<=capacity; otherwise status=rejected. Accepted add status=accepted. Cancel removes current id with status=cancelled, absent id=missing. Run takes the job with smallest deadline, breaking ties by earlier accepted insertion, with status=ran; empty run status=empty. Advance status=advanced. IDs may be reused after removal. Output {status,ran:id_or_null,pending:[ids in insertion order],bytes:sum_size,now}. Expiry never counts as ran. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}; initial state is null. Only the current event is available; each named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"run"}. Inputs have at most eight single lowercase ASCII-letter identifiers, safe integer quantities and at most 48 events. Return exactly the documented output fields after every event; state representation is unrestricted JSON. All identifiers and numeric fields shown in event forms are present; quantities and all intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. Regimes vary event order and timing: ordinary uses moderate capacity, boundary tests equality/empty cases, adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events, and shift uses smaller capacities or larger costs/delays within the same semantics. Generator regimes: Boundary capacity=2; shift capacity=4 versus ordinary 7, sizes 2..6 instead of 1..5, deadline gaps 0..2 instead of 0..5, and clock steps 0..5 instead of 0..3. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Wetland flood storage
matchedCard.relation: Temporary storage and slow release can spread an incoming surge over time and reduce a downstream peak. In a simplified flow balance, retained quantity changes with inflow and outflow; delaying movement does not by itself remove the incoming quantity.
assumptions: Release or another accounted outflow can restore capacity between surges.
Any other gain or loss is included in the flow balance.
matchedCard.boundary: Storage alone cannot absorb a sustained excess of inflow indefinitely. A reduced peak is not evidence that the total incoming quantity disappeared.
matchedCard.source_fact: EPA describes wetlands trapping and slowly releasing water, slowing runoff, and storing peak flows. The finite-capacity balance is an explicitly stated abstraction of storage behavior.

sources.title: Incorporating Wetland Restoration and Protection in Planning Documents

shuffledCard.label: Theatrical lighting cue tracking
shuffledCard.relation: A value entered in a sequence persists through later positions that contain no replacement for it. A new entry can therefore alter later states. A cue-only change limits that propagation by restoring the prior downstream value at the next position.
assumptions: The sequence uses tracking rather than independent complete states.
Explicit changes can be distinguished from values inherited from earlier positions.
shuffledCard.boundary: An absent change is not an explicit reset. Forward-tracking and cue-only editing have different scopes and cannot be assumed interchangeable.
shuffledCard.source_fact: ETC documents values tracking forward through cues and a cue-only operation that prevents an inserted or merged change from altering subsequent cues.

initial.explanation: The rule is: before each event, discard queued jobs whose deadline is at or before now; an advance also discards after increasing now. Add accepts exactly when the ID is absent, its deadline is later than now, and capacity remains sufficient. Run selects minimum deadline, then insertion order. For example, changing the first accepted add's bytes from 1 to 2 violates conservation and capacity accounting.
initial.mapping: now is the clock; jobs contain id, size, deadline, and insertion sequence; bytes is the sum of queued sizes; pending is queued IDs in sequence order. Status and ran describe only the current event.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated legal-event and safe-integer constraints. State is trusted only as state previously returned by this function.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let c=input.config.capacity,n=0,q=[],seq=0,eq=()=>{q=q.filter(x=>x.deadline>n)},mk=(s,r)=>({status:s,ran:r==null?null:r,pending:q.map(x=>x.id),bytes:q.reduce((a,x)=>a+x.size,0),now:n});for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let e=input.events[i];eq();let s,r=null;if(e.type==='add'){if(q.some(x=>x.id===e.id)||e.deadline<=n||q.reduce((a,x)=>a+x.size,0)+e.size>c)s='rejected';else{q.push({id:e.id,size:e.size,deadline:e.deadline,seq:seq++});s='accepted'}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){let k=q.findIndex(x=>x.id===e.id);if(k<0)s='missing';else{q.splice(k,1);s='cancelled'}}else if(e.type==='advance'){n+=e.dt;eq();s='advanced'}else{if(!q.length)s='empty';else{let k=0;for(let j=1;j<q.length;j++)if(q[j].deadline<q[k].deadline||q[j].deadline===q[k].deadline&&q[j].seq<q[k].seq)k=j;r=q[k].id;q.splice(k,1);s='ran'}}let z=mk(s,r),o=output[i];if(JSON.stringify(z)!==JSON.stringify(o))return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains the current clock and queued jobs in insertion order. Expired jobs are removed before every event and immediately after advancing. Adds require an unused queued ID, a deadline strictly after now, and sufficient capacity. Runs select the earliest deadline, preserving insertion order on ties; cancellation and capacity accounting update the queue accordingly.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{now:0,jobs:[]},now=s.now,jobs=s.jobs.slice();const expire=()=>{jobs=jobs.filter(j=>j.deadline>now)};expire();let status,ran=null;if(event.type==='add'){let bytes=0,used=false;for(let j of jobs){bytes+=j.size;if(j.id===event.id)used=true}if(used||event.deadline<=now||bytes+event.size>config.capacity)status='rejected';else{jobs.push({id:event.id,size:event.size,deadline:event.deadline});status='accepted'}}else if(event.type==='cancel'){let k=jobs.findIndex(j=>j.id===event.id);if(k<0)status='missing';else{jobs.splice(k,1);status='cancelled'}}else if(event.type==='advance'){now+=event.dt;expire();status='advanced'}else{if(!jobs.length)status='empty';else{let k=0;for(let i=1;i<jobs.length;i++)if(jobs[i].deadline<jobs[k].deadline)k=i;ran=jobs[k].id;jobs.splice(k,1);status='ran'}}let bytes=0;for(let j of jobs)bytes+=j.size;return{state:{now:now,jobs:jobs},output:{status:status,ran:ran,pending:jobs.map(j=>j.id),bytes:bytes,now:now}}}

initial.explanation: Maintain the current clock and queued jobs. Before each event, discard expired jobs; advancing also discards jobs after increasing the clock. Accepted jobs consume capacity, cancellation and execution release their sizes, and execution selects earliest deadline then insertion order.
initial.mapping: config.capacity maps to maximum queued bytes; state.now maps to time; state.jobs stores id, size, deadline, and insertion order; output.pending and output.bytes summarize queued jobs; output.ran identifies only a job executed by run.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated event and numeric validity constraints. JSON state is private to this implementation and is returned unchanged in meaning between calls.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let c=input.config.capacity,n=0,j=[],t=0;function x(){j=j.filter(q=>q.d>t)}for(let k=0;k<output.length;k++){let e=input.events[k],o=output[k];x();let r=null,s='';if(e.type==='add'){if(j.some(q=>q.id===e.id)||n+e.size>c||e.deadline<=t)s='rejected';else{s='accepted';j.push({id:e.id,size:e.size,d:e.deadline,ix:k});n+=e.size}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){let z=j.findIndex(q=>q.id===e.id);if(z<0)s='missing';else{s='cancelled';n-=j[z].size;j.splice(z,1)}}else if(e.type==='advance'){s='advanced';t+=e.dt;x()}else{s='empty';if(j.length){let z=0;for(let i=1;i<j.length;i++)if(j[i].d<j[z].d||j[i].d===j[z].d&&j[i].ix<j[z].ix)z=i;r=j[z].id;n-=j[z].size;j.splice(z,1);s='ran'}}if(o.status!==s||o.now!==t||o.bytes!==n||o.ran!==r||o.pending.length!==j.length) return false;for(let i=0;i<j.length;i++)if(o.pending[i]!==j[i].id)return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintain clock, queued jobs, total bytes, and a monotonic insertion sequence. Expire jobs before every event and again after advancing. Add checks current identity, deadline, and capacity; cancel and run release bytes. Run selects the earliest deadline, then earliest accepted sequence.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{now:0,jobs:[],bytes:0,seq:0},now=s.now,j=(s.jobs||[]).map(x=>({id:x.id,size:x.size,deadline:x.deadline,seq:x.seq})),bytes=s.bytes==null?j.reduce((a,x)=>a+x.size,0):s.bytes,seq=s.seq||0;function expire(){for(let i=j.length-1;i>=0;i--)if(j[i].deadline<=now){bytes-=j[i].size;j.splice(i,1)}}expire();let status,ran=null;if(event.type==='add'){let exists=false;for(let i=0;i<j.length;i++)if(j[i].id===event.id){exists=true;break}if(exists||event.deadline<=now||bytes+event.size>config.capacity)status='rejected';else{status='accepted';j.push({id:event.id,size:event.size,deadline:event.deadline,seq:++seq});bytes+=event.size}}else if(event.type==='cancel'){let i=-1;for(let k=0;k<j.length;k++)if(j[k].id===event.id){i=k;break}if(i<0)status='missing';else{status='cancelled';bytes-=j[i].size;j.splice(i,1)}}else if(event.type==='advance'){status='advanced';now+=event.dt;expire()}else{if(!j.length)status='empty';else{let i=0;for(let k=1;k<j.length;k++)if(j[k].deadline<j[i].deadline||j[k].deadline===j[i].deadline&&j[k].seq<j[i].seq)i=k;ran=j[i].id;bytes-=j[i].size;j.splice(i,1);status='ran'}}return{state:{now:now,jobs:j,bytes:bytes,seq:seq},output:{status:status,ran:ran,pending:j.map(x=>x.id),bytes:bytes,now:now}}}

initial.explanation: A queued job remains eligible until its deadline, while expiration is applied before each event and immediately after time advances. Accepted jobs retain insertion order for deadline ties.
initial.mapping: config.capacity bounds queued bytes; state tracks now, queued jobs, and insertion sequence; event mutates only the current queue and clock; output is a snapshot after processing.
initial.assumptions: Events and quantities satisfy the stated public preconditions. State is trusted only as the state returned by this program.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){let c=input.config.capacity,n=0,q=[],seq=0;function exp(){q=q.filter(x=>x.d>n)}function snap(s,r){let b=0;for(let x of q)b+=x.z;return s&&output[i].status===s&&output[i].now===n&&output[i].bytes===b&&output[i].ran===r&&JSON.stringify(output[i].pending)===JSON.stringify(q.map(x=>x.id))}for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let e=input.events[i];exp();let r=null,s;if(e.type==='add'){if(q.some(x=>x.id===e.id)||e.deadline<=n||q.reduce((a,x)=>a+x.z,0)+e.size>c)s='rejected';else{q.push({id:e.id,z:e.size,d:e.deadline,k:seq++});s='accepted'}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){let j=q.findIndex(x=>x.id===e.id);if(j<0)s='missing';else{q.splice(j,1);s='cancelled'}}else if(e.type==='advance'){n+=e.dt;exp();s='advanced'}else{if(!q.length)s='empty';else{let j=0;for(let k=1;k<q.length;k++)if(q[k].d<q[j].d||q[k].d===q[j].d&&q[k].k<q[j].k)j=k;r=q[j].id;q.splice(j,1);s='ran'}}if(!snap(s,r))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{now:0,jobs:[],seq:0},q=s.jobs;function expire(){s.jobs=q=q.filter(x=>x.deadline>s.now)}function bytes(){let n=0;for(let x of q)n+=x.size;return n}expire();let t=event.type,st,ran=null;if(t==='add'){if(q.some(x=>x.id===event.id)||event.deadline<=s.now||bytes()+event.size>config.capacity)st='rejected';else{q.push({id:event.id,size:event.size,deadline:event.deadline,seq:s.seq++});st='accepted'}}else if(t==='cancel'){let i=q.findIndex(x=>x.id===event.id);if(i<0)st='missing';else{q.splice(i,1);st='cancelled'}}else if(t==='advance'){s.now+=event.dt;expire();st='advanced'}else if(t==='run'){if(!q.length)st='empty';else{let i=0;for(let j=1;j<q.length;j++)if(q[j].deadline<q[i].deadline||q[j].deadline===q[i].deadline&&q[j].seq<q[i].seq)i=j;ran=q[i].id;q.splice(i,1);st='ran'}}return{state:s,output:{status:st,ran:ran,pending:q.map(x=>x.id),bytes:bytes(),now:s.now}}}

final.explanation: Maintains the current time, queued jobs, total insertion sequence, and applies expiration before every event and immediately after advances. Adds require a unique queued ID, a future deadline, and sufficient capacity. Runs select minimum deadline, preserving accepted insertion order for ties. Each response is a complete snapshot with exactly the required fields.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{now:0,jobs:[],seq:0},q=s.jobs;function expire(){q=s.jobs=s.jobs.filter(x=>x.deadline>s.now)}function bytes(){let n=0;for(let x of q)n+=x.size;return n}expire();let type=event.type,status,ran=null;if(type==='add'){if(q.some(x=>x.id===event.id)||event.deadline<=s.now||bytes()+event.size>config.capacity)status='rejected';else{q.push({id:event.id,size:event.size,deadline:event.deadline,seq:s.seq++});status='accepted'}}else if(type==='cancel'){let i=q.findIndex(x=>x.id===event.id);if(i<0)status='missing';else{q.splice(i,1);status='cancelled'}}else if(type==='advance'){s.now+=event.dt;expire();status='advanced'}else if(type==='run'){if(!q.length)status='empty';else{let i=0;for(let j=1;j<q.length;j++)if(q[j].deadline<q[i].deadline||q[j].deadline===q[i].deadline&&q[j].seq<q[i].seq)i=j;ran=q[i].id;q.splice(i,1);status='ran'}}return{state:s,output:{status,ran,pending:q.map(x=>x.id),bytes:bytes(),now:s.now}}}
